ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ray-queried latent autoencoder for shape and glossy appearance
PROPOSAL: Encode a point sample of each mesh, plus colors seen from posed renders, into 512 latent tokens. A transformer decoder answers two query types: occupancy at a 3D point and RGB along a camera ray. Train on 30,000 Objaverse assets with their metallic and glossy materials intact, skipping watertight conversion, using three seeds, and keep 1,000 assets held out. Report Chamfer distance, F-score and PSNR on novel views.
CONTROLS: A geometry-only autoencoder with the same encoder, for shape accuracy; a decoder blind to ray direction, to isolate the view-dependent gain; smaller and bigger latents to check sensitivity.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Shape quality should stay within noise of the geometry-only model while PSNR on specular objects improves by about 2 dB over the direction-blind decoder. It fails if the encoder discards highlights.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint shape-and-appearance tokens from posed renders at corpus breadth
PROPOSAL: Fit the latent model on 160,000 Objaverse assets, converting each mesh into surface samples with colors taken from 48 posed renders. Train at token counts of 256, 512 and 1024 with two seeds, decoding occupancy and ray color through one shared transformer. Score the checkpoints on three held-out splits (random, glossy-only, translucent-only) using Chamfer distance, F-score and PSNR on novel views, then report per-split tables and per-seed spread.
CONTROLS: A geometry-only autoencoder per token count; a ray-direction-blind decoder per token count; a color-only decoder; evaluation under four lighting conditions per object, with 8 viewpoints.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Geometry should match the geometry-only models, and glossy-split PSNR should beat the blind decoder by roughly 2 dB. The gain may vanish on the translucent split, where renders carry little directional signal, and per-seed spread will show how stable the ordering is.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does a ray-conditioned color head recover highlights from a compact code?
PROPOSAL: Run a pilot on 4,000 reflective and rough objects, each rendered from 12 views. Compress each into 128 latent tokens, then compare two appearance decoders: an MLP that takes the camera ray as input, and a head that predicts spherical harmonic coefficients per surface point. Both read the same shape latent and are trained with two seeds. Measure highlight position error and PSNR inside masked specular regions of 400 held-out objects.
CONTROLS: An appearance decoder with no view input; a decoder trained on diffuse-only renders of these objects; the shape latent frozen versus jointly tuned; 64 and 256 tokens as size checks.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: The ray-conditioned head should localize highlights more precisely than low-order spherical harmonics, with a PSNR gain near 1.5 dB inside specular regions. If both heads tie, view dependence is probably carried by the shape latent rather than the decoder.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Render-resolution and viewpoint-count analysis of an appearance latent on mirror-like assets
PROPOSAL: Assemble 40,000 objects and render each from 24, 48 or 96 viewpoints at two image sizes. Learn a 256-token latent per object and decode color through a ray MLP and a spherical harmonic head, trained with three seeds. Compare highlight position error and PSNR inside specular masks of 4,000 held-out objects for the six render settings and both heads, keeping a table per setting and a plot of error against viewpoint count.
CONTROLS: Decoders without view input per render setting; diffuse-only training renders; frozen versus jointly tuned shape latents; a reference built from a sparse set of viewpoints; a half-resolution run.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: The ray MLP should beat spherical harmonics by around 1.5 dB near highlights, and gains should flatten beyond 48 viewpoints. If the settings tie, the decoder choice matters more than data density, so the cheapest setting would then suffice for later work.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Decoding a compact latent into view-dependent 3D Gaussians
PROPOSAL: Train an encoder that maps 20,000 posed multiview image sets directly to 1,024 latent tokens, with no radiance-field fitting stage. A decoder emits 4,000 3D Gaussians per object, each with opacity and a small neural color function that depends on viewing direction. Supervise only with rendering losses from the posed images, run two seeds, then test on 500 unseen objects with PSNR, LPIPS and depth error.
CONTROLS: A decoder emitting view-independent color per Gaussian; a per-object optimized Gaussian fit as an upper bound; a geometry-only latent for depth accuracy.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: View-dependent color should lift PSNR by 1 to 2 dB on glossy objects over view-independent color, while depth error stays near the geometry-only latent. The decoder may fail on thin structures where the primitive count runs short.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Direct multiview-to-Gaussian autoencoding with directional color
PROPOSAL: Use 90,000 posed multiview sets and train an encoder producing 1,024 latent tokens per object. The decoder outputs 16,000 Gaussians with view-dependent color functions, supervised with rendering losses at four image resolutions and trained with three seeds. Test on 2,000 unseen objects with PSNR, LPIPS, depth error and normal error at three camera radii, and break results down by object category and material label.
CONTROLS: View-independent color Gaussians; per-object optimization with 5,000 steps; a geometry-only latent; a decoder with twice the primitives.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Directional color should add 1 to 2 dB PSNR on glossy objects, with depth error close to the geometry-only latent. Doubling the primitives probably brings little once thin parts are covered, so the seed spread should be small next to the directional-color gain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training the latent from raw meshes with no watertight preprocessing
PROPOSAL: Compare two data pipelines for one geometry-and-appearance autoencoder. In the first, surface points and normals are sampled directly from raw, often non-watertight meshes of 12,000 Objaverse assets. In the second, each mesh is first converted into a watertight signed distance field. Both feed 512 latent tokens and a ray-conditioned color decoder, trained with three seeds, and are scored on 600 held-out assets with Chamfer distance and PSNR.
CONTROLS: The watertight pipeline as baseline; a raw-mesh model that drops the normals; a model trained only on the 7,000 assets where conversion succeeds.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Raw-surface training should match watertight geometry within 5% on Chamfer distance and avoid the failures where conversion breaks thin parts. It could lose accuracy on assets with inconsistent normals.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Raw-mesh versus converted-mesh training of an appearance-aware latent
PROPOSAL: Build four training corpora from 60,000 Objaverse assets: raw surface samples, watertight signed distance fields, voxel occupancy at resolution 64, and a union of the three. Train a 512-token geometry-plus-appearance autoencoder on each of the four with two seeds, then score 3,000 held-out assets on Chamfer distance, F-score and PSNR, and record where conversion fails, listing the failure types per corpus plus the share of assets each pipeline loses.
CONTROLS: Normals dropped from the raw-mesh input; a model trained only on the assets where conversion works; a bigger latent for each corpus, to see whether the gap depends on capacity.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Raw surface training should land within 5% of watertight Chamfer distance and keep thin parts intact. Gains from the union corpus are likely small relative to seed spread.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Single-image generation of latent 3D objects with a flow transformer
PROPOSAL: Train a rectified-flow transformer on the latent codes of 100,000 objects, conditioned on DINOv2 features from one rendered view, with two seeds. Decode each sampled latent into occupancy and view-dependent color in one stage. Evaluate on 1,000 unseen test images with Chamfer distance against ground truth, CLIP similarity on novel views, and a reflection score comparing highlight positions to the input image.
CONTROLS: Conditioning on CLIP image embeddings instead of DINOv2; a generator using view-independent color in the decoder; a two-stage baseline that predicts occupancy first.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The one-stage model should match the two-stage baseline on shape and win on the reflection score by a clear gap. Failure is likely on objects whose input view shows little of the reverse side.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Image-conditioned flow generation of shape and appearance latents at corpus scale
PROPOSAL: Train a rectified-flow transformer with 1.1B parameters on codes of 350,000 objects, conditioned on DINOv2 features of one render, with three seeds. Decode in one stage into occupancy and directional color, then evaluate Chamfer distance, CLIP similarity and a highlight-position score on 4,000 test images, at two sampling-step counts and two guidance scales, reporting a table for each pairing and the spread over seeds.
CONTROLS: CLIP embedding conditioning; a view-independent color decoder; a two-stage baseline predicting occupancy first; a 300M transformer.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: One-stage generation should tie the two-stage baseline on geometry and lead on highlight position. Gains from the bigger transformer may be modest relative to data scale.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Generation in arbitrary object orientation from an input photo
PROPOSAL: Test whether latents without a canonical grid let the generator place objects in the pose seen in the input image. Train on 25,000 objects whose orientation is randomized, conditioned on one rendered view, with three seeds. Measure rotation error against the ground-truth pose, Chamfer distance after alignment, and PSNR from the input viewpoint on 1,000 test images.
CONTROLS: A baseline generator trained on canonically oriented data followed by an alignment step; a version trained on canonical data with no alignment; random-orientation training with the pose given as an explicit input.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Rotation error should stay under 10 degrees for most test objects without post-processing, beating the canonical-plus-alignment pipeline on symmetric parts. Pose may be ambiguous for near-symmetric objects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Orientation-free image-to-3D generation under five pose regimes
PROPOSAL: Train generators on 70,000 objects under five orientation regimes: canonical, randomized, randomized with pose input, canonical with a learned aligner, and a mixture. Condition on one render, use two seeds, then measure rotation error, Chamfer distance after alignment and PSNR from the input viewpoint on 2,500 test images at two image resolutions, splitting results by object category and by symmetry class.
CONTROLS: Canonical generation followed by alignment; canonical with no alignment; every regime scored with and without a symmetry-aware rotation metric; a canonical run that receives the pose as an explicit input.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Randomized training should give rotation errors below 10 degrees and beat the aligner on symmetric parts. The mixture regime may add little over randomization alone.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Lighting fidelity of generated objects under relit input images
PROPOSAL: Check whether generated objects reflect the illumination in the input photo. Take 200 test objects, render each under 4 environment maps, and generate a 3D object from each render using a trained image-conditioned latent generator with three seeds. Then render the result under the original environment map at 2 camera elevations and score PSNR and highlight-direction angle error against the input view.
CONTROLS: The same generator fed with the diffuse-only form of each input; a generator conditioned on a different environment map than the input; a shape-only model; a generator trained without relit examples.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Highlight direction error should fall by about a third relative to diffuse-only inputs. The model might bake the dataset's average lighting into its outputs and ignore the input environment.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Environment-map robustness of image-to-3D appearance under a lighting library
PROPOSAL: Use 1,500 test objects, rendering each under 16 environment maps, and generate a 3D object from each render with an image-conditioned latent generator, trained with two seeds. Re-render the outputs under the source map and score PSNR and highlight-direction angle error, then group results by roughness bin and map type, keeping a table per map and per camera elevation.
CONTROLS: Diffuse-only input forms; a generator conditioned on mismatched environment maps; a shape-only model; an identity baseline copying the input pixels; a version fed mismatched roughness labels; a coarse-lighting variant.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Highlight direction error should shrink by about a third against diffuse-only inputs. Results by map type may show larger errors under harsh point-like lighting, with seed spread expected to stay small.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: One-stage versus two-stage generation of view-dependent 3D objects
PROPOSAL: Train two generators on 200,000 objects with equal parameter counts of 1B. The one-stage model denoises a joint latent and decodes shape and directional color together. The two-stage model first predicts coarse occupancy and then fills appearance. Condition both on one rendered image, use two seeds, and compare Chamfer distance, novel-view CLIP score and highlight position error on 3,000 held-out images.
CONTROLS: A geometry-only generator for shape accuracy; one-stage training with view-independent color; matched sampling steps of 50 for the two generators; inference without image conditioning.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: The one-stage model should match shape accuracy while improving highlight position error over the two-stage model. If the coarse occupancy stage already encodes appearance cues, the two-stage model may close the gap.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Parameter-count comparison of one-stage and two-stage generators for directional appearance
PROPOSAL: Train both generator types at 300M, 1B and 3B parameters on 800,000 objects from three corpora, conditioned on a single render, with three seeds for the smaller sizes. Compare Chamfer distance, novel-view CLIP score and highlight position error on 8,000 held-out images, using two sampling step counts, and splitting the scores by object category and by material class.
CONTROLS: A geometry-only generator per size; one-stage training with view-independent color; an unconditional run per size; identical sampling steps for the two generator types; a frozen-encoder variant of each generator.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: At matched size the one-stage design should keep shape accuracy and improve highlight error, with gains growing slowly with size. The two-stage model may close the gap if its coarse stage encodes appearance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Token budget versus fidelity for a compact appearance-aware latent
PROPOSAL: Measure the trade-off between latent size and reconstruction for a geometry-plus-appearance autoencoder using 128, 256, 512 and 1024 tokens on 30,000 objects, with two seeds. Compare against a sparse voxel structured latent built from foundation-model features, reporting Chamfer distance, PSNR on specular regions, and memory per object on 1,000 held-out assets.
CONTROLS: The sparse voxel latent at matched memory; a token-count-matched geometry-only autoencoder; a version with view-independent color.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Reconstruction should saturate near 512 tokens, and specular PSNR should exceed the sparse voxel baseline by about 3 dB at equal memory. Thin or translucent objects may keep improving past the saturation point.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latent size and encoder choice for joint geometry and view-dependent color
PROPOSAL: Train autoencoders with 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024 and 2048 tokens on 120,000 objects, using two encoder types, a point transformer and a multiview image encoder, with three seeds. Compare against a sparse voxel baseline from foundation-model features on Chamfer distance, specular PSNR and memory, scored on 4,000 held-out assets.
CONTROLS: A sparse voxel latent at matched memory; geometry-only autoencoders at each size; view-independent color versions at each size.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Quality should saturate near 512 tokens and the specular PSNR should beat sparse voxels by about 3 dB at equal memory. The multiview encoder may help on translucent objects and thin parts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Material-stratified evaluation of view-dependent reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Build a test split of 300 objects labelled mirror-like, glossy, rough or translucent from their material parameters. Evaluate a pretrained joint latent autoencoder and a geometry-only reference on each stratum, with three seeds of the sampling of views, using Chamfer distance, PSNR and a highlight sharpness score on novel views, and report where the gap to the geometry-only model is largest.
CONTROLS: A diffuse-color variant of the joint model; a stratum-matched random subset of 300 objects; the geometry-only reference reconstruction.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: The joint model should match geometry within 3% on all strata and lead on PSNR mostly for mirror-like and glossy objects. Translucent objects are the most likely to show a geometry penalty.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Stratified material benchmark of joint latents with viewpoint rings
PROPOSAL: Create a test split of 2,000 objects spanning five material labels and 4 roughness bins. Evaluate a pretrained joint autoencoder and a geometry-only reference with Chamfer distance, PSNR and highlight sharpness on novel views from 12 viewpoint rings, with two seeds for view sampling, and give the stratum where the joint model trails most.
CONTROLS: A diffuse-color variant of the joint model; random subsets of equal size per stratum; geometry-only reconstruction on the same rings.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Geometry should stay within 3% of the reference on every stratum, with the PSNR lead concentrated in mirror-like and glossy classes. Translucent objects are the likeliest to show a geometry penalty.
